answer: The basalt multiplier is published, charged in ledge, and quill lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 11 for each member already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A burst of registrations hence prices itself out, since the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 4605 identities would post 4194 proofs and burn roughly 69 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
